findings: avoiding_interval_side_iff uses the actual consecutive positions A.val=s.val and B.val=s.val+1 and I.left<I.right. It proves that avoiding both is equivalent to the entire interval ending at or before A, or starting at or after B. Non-strict outer inequalities deliberately retain intervals ending exactly at A or starting exactly at B. There is no omitted discrete interval crossing the gap between those consecutive positions.

On the first side, both endpoint representatives are at most s.val and collapse_val leaves both unchanged. On the second side, both are greater than s.val and collapse subtracts one from each. The proof has I.left.val>=s.val+1>=1, so natural-number subtraction does not introduce a truncation artifact. The same endpoint difference is therefore the actual BoundaryInterval.leaves on each side; this is a numeric proof, not a general claim that arbitrary order embeddings preserve leaf counts.

collapseInterval_unit_avoiding obtains equality of endpoint differences, uses strictness of both actual intervals, and proves equivalence of the two successor-endpoint tests. Unfolding boundaryUnitArray then identifies the corresponding if-then-one-else-zero entries over any CommRing. Neither inverse-of-two assumptions, nonzero scalar factors nor an assumed transform equation enter the argument.

The avoidance premise implies the stated hI by the existing duplicate-interval definition; carrying that proof for the dependent collapseInterval does not narrow the source domain. Arbitrary distinguished positions include s=0 and s=n-1, all avoiding A/B endpoint cases, and source n=3. The body does not evaluate a degenerate collapsed interval or invoke an amplitude at a smaller arity.
